title: Chapter 18: Livestream
html:
Only one person in the building fit that description: the elderly man who shared a room with the “landlord.”

That doesn’t add up. According to the reports, the owner should be an old man, but the person who received me is only middle-aged.Chen Ge got up and pressed his ear to the wall. The television next door was still blaring, now playing a commercial.

Wouldn’t most people change the channel during a commercial break? It’s been going for several minutes.He leaned closer to the wall.Maybe I missed something.

He cleared his thoughts and arranged the clues again from the beginning.Right after I entered my room, I heard a plate break next door. Then the landlord started berating the old man, and it only stopped after the television was turned up. The old man can barely move, so the landlord must have raised the volume. But why?

Chen Ge narrowed his eyes as a troubling possibility occurred to him.Could the landlord be mistreating the old man? Maybe the television is there to drown out whatever is happening next door.

The more he considered it, the less far-fetched it seemed.The plate broke almost the moment I moved in. Was that really a coincidence? Could the old man have been trying to get my attention? It was only a broken plate, yet the landlord became furious. Maybe he was worried I would notice something.

But what is he afraid of? And why would the old man need help?

Then Chen Ge remembered another detail he had dismissed earlier. While berating the old man, the landlord had slipped into curses from another region.

The family who died here were locals, but this landlord isn’t from Jiujiang. He probably isn’t related to the old man at all.

Normally, a man would not hand control of his property to a complete stranger unless there were special circumstances. What if the limping man took over the building and is keeping the old man under his control? He could be an unscrupulous caretaker—or someone connected to the old case.

Either possibility was bad news for Chen Ge.

His hands curled into fists.That would also explain why he was listening outside my door earlier. He wanted to know how much I had figured out.

A thin sheen of sweat formed on Chen Ge’s forehead. He was no detective; most of his ideas came from crime dramas he had watched on television.

What am I supposed to do? Confront him now? No. That would be reckless, especially if I’m wrong.Chen Ge paced the room, trying to think.

Should I test him somehow? No, that could give me away. He might have accomplices, and I’m here alone. More importantly, I have no proof—only guesses. The mission brought me here to identify whoever was responsible for the old case. I should focus on that first.

Chen Ge was still wrestling with the problem when the television next door abruptly went silent. The building became unnervingly quiet.

What happened?He eased his door open and crouched low enough to look toward the neighboring room. No light showed beneath its door.

Going to sleep at eight?Chen Ge crept toward the landlord’s door, then abruptly realized how suspicious he must look. He glanced around, thought better of it, and returned to his room.

My theory might be completely wrong. If only I had someone better at this kind of analysis.Chen Ge lay back on the bed and took out his phone. Aside from Xu Wan, there were not many people in his contacts whom he spoke to regularly.

Good grief. I really need more friends.

After thinking it over, he remembered the only person he knew with even a vaguely relevant background: He San, the medical student who had fainted inside his Haunted House.

A medical student should at least be better at logical analysis than I am.He opened the video-sharing app and found nearly twenty private messages waiting for him. One was from a studio affiliated with the platform, inviting him to work with them.

Some kind of talent scout?Chen Ge had no time for that. He scrolled past the messages in search of He San’s account and put the invitation out of his mind.

A few minutes later, however, the studio messaged him again.

“You there? We saw your video. It has a lot of potential.”

“Would you be interested in working with us?”

“We can connect you with some of the platform’s top streamers and help increase your exposure.”

“It’s difficult to build an audience alone. Most successful streamers rely on teams and connections.”

“It’s a strong offer. Think it over.”

“You there?”

The relentless notifications irritated Chen Ge. He was in the middle of a deeply unsettling night, and these people were trying to sell him a business arrangement. At last, he replied with a single message: “AFK.”

“You’ve got a sense of humor. Seriously, though, consider our offer. All you need to do is add our studio logo to your videos. In return, we’ll help promote you and grow your audience.”

“Sorry, I’m not interested right now.” Chen Ge thought that was polite enough. Someone with less patience might already have blocked them.

“Your short video could go viral, but ‘could’ is the important word. This platform gets an enormous number of uploads every day, and you were fortunate enough to stand out once. Online audiences move quickly. There is always something newer competing for their attention. If you don’t build on this momentum, your video will soon be buried.”

“We can talk another time. I’m busy.” Chen Ge finally found He San’s account.

“What could be more important than making money? If you’re hesitant about joining us, we can discuss another arrangement. We’d also be willing to pay for your content or your filming methods.”

That was enough. Chen Ge blocked the account and sent He San a message instead.

To his surprise, He San replied within seconds. “Boss! I’ve been waiting for you to post another video!”

“Hold on. I need to ask you something more important.” After getting He San’s number, Chen Ge called him and quietly explained what had happened since arriving at the apartments.
